  • Industry observers note that comfort aside, noise cancellation is another area where these headphones deliver, doing a particularly good job of reducing lower-frequency rumble and background chatter, though some higher-pitched voices can still come through, notes this PCMag review.

It has been revealed that bose’s second-generation QuietComfort Headphones are 45% off right now, down to $199 for Black Friday, saving you $160 and bringing them to their lowest price yet. Colors include in Dewdrop Mint, Eucalyptus Green, and Hazelnut Taupe. Weighing around 8.1 ounces, they’re among the lightest premium noise-canceling headphones, with generously padded earcups and a cushioned headband that spreads pressure without gripping too tightly, making them comfortable to wear for extended periods. They’re also easy to pack for travel, as the earcups fold and swivel for storage in the included hard-shell carrying case. The removable earpads are another welcome touch, since you can replace them as they wear down without having to retire the entire pair.

Industry observers note that comfort aside, noise cancellation is another area where these headphones deliver, doing a particularly good job of reducing lower-frequency rumble and background chatter, though some higher-pitched voices can still come through, notes this PCMag review. As for their sound profile, it leans warm and bass-forward, with deep lows that suit bass-heavy genres, while the companion app adds Bose Immersive Audio for spatial sound and lets you create customized listening profiles—the three-band EQ is fairly basic, though, so anyone who likes fine-tuning their sound may find the adjustment options limiting.

Sources indicate that connectivity, too, brings some useful upgrades over the previous generation, including Bluetooth 5.4, multipoint pairing for two devices, Google Fast Pair, and lossless audio over USB-C. That same USB-C port lets you charge the headphones while you listen, and the included USB-C-to-3.5mm cable covers standard headphone jacks, including the ones on in-flight entertainment systems. That said, battery life is less impressive, topping out at 24 hours with ANC enabled, although a 15-minute charge adds around 2.5 hours of playback. Wireless audio is also limited to the standard AAC and SBC codecs, with no support for the higher-quality aptX Adaptive—a feature available on Bose’s QuietComfort Ultra Headphones.

  • Industry observers note that JBL's Go 4 is a small speaker, but it gets surprisingly loud—especially for a speaker at this price point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that while tech can get pretty expensive, especially in our current "RAMageddon" era, there are still plenty of affordable devices out there. The problem, of course, isn't quantity, but quality: Buying a tech item for under $50 is risky, since many of these products are made as cheaply as possible. If you're looking for a portable Bluetooth speaker, for instance, you don't want to buy something with poor sound quality, or that doesn't easily connect to your devices, or that breaks unexpectedly.

You don't need to worry about any of that with the JBL Go 4. This is a solid portable speaker that just so happens to have an MSRP of $49.95. It's so good, I named it Lifehacker's best gift under $50, as its price, excellent sound quality, and feature set make it a great option for most anyone on your list. It's an even better buy during Black Friday, too: Right now, you can pick up the JBL Go 4 for as low as $31.95, 36% off the original retail price.

Industry observers note that JBL's Go 4 is a small speaker, but it gets surprisingly loud—especially for a speaker at this price point. Like other JBL speakers, it places a particular emphasis on bass. This is a tiny speaker, so don't expect a subwoofer on the go, but not only will it let you hear the bass in your music, it is noticeably punchy. JBL advertises seven hours of playtime on a single charge here, which is often plenty for taking the speaker out and about for the day. You can net an additional two hours of if you engage "Playtime Boost." JBL doesn't specify how this works, but it likely cuts some of the frequencies here to save on battery life. And, since it's 1P67-rated against dust and water, it's a great choice for outdoor use.

It has been revealed that perhaps my favorite thing about the JBL Go 4 is that it supports Auracast. That means you can easily connect to any other Auracast-compatible JBL speaker using the Auracast button on each device. I've used this before at parties and gatherings for an impromptu multi-speaker setup. Since JBL is so popular, it's not impractical to assume one or two other people at the function might have a similar speaker you can connect to, or if you know friends or family members have JBL speakers of their own, you can coordinate these setups ahead of time.

Industry observers note that this discount is only available on specific colors of the Go 4, at least on Amazon: Black, White, Blue, Purple, Red, and "Squad." Black and Orange, Pink, and Sand are all still $49.95. Again, the JBL Go 4 is absolutely worth the $50 MSRP, but unless you're married to one of those three colors, it's even better at a discount.

Recent findings suggest that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

Sources indicate that the best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Some other tips are making sure you're not being sold an older or cheaper version and always reading reviews.

Beats has a long history of making on-ear headphones that stand with the plushest and best-sounding cans on the market. As Black Friday deals are here, it's a great time to upgrade: Walmart has discounted the Beats Solo 4 by more than 50% to $99.95 (originally $199.95); the sale applies to the black, pink, and slate blue variants.

These headphones don’t have ANC, just passive isolation, but they still deliver solid sound, comfort, and strong battery life. They use physical controls and support one-touch pairing with most Apple devices, as well as hands-free Siri. The Solo 4 headphones are compatible with Bluetooth 5.3 and work with the AAC and SBC codecs. They also support wired audio via 3.5mm or USB-C.

According to recent reports, the headphones last around 50 hours per charge (about 10 hours longer than their predecessor), and 10 minutes of charging gives you around five hours of playback, with a full recharge taking approximately two hours. In its review, PCMag describes the sound as “sculpted with accentuated bass and highs.".

Although they lack ANC and adjustable EQ, these headphones still have plenty of extra features for Apple owners, and those shortcomings are much easier to forgive at 50% off. For $99, the Beats Solo 4 headphones are a compact and well-equipped option for casual listening, with long battery life and that classic Beats aesthetic.

‘Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles’ Officially Begins a Brutal New Era in Stunning Preview

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1418 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 40 Years ago, the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles made their debut.
  • Starting with January's Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #25, the series will be penned by Matthew Rosenberg, who's written Punisher, Batman, and Spawn, as well as the indie crime comic 4 Kids Walk Into a Bank, while Juann Cabal, a veteran of Guardians of the Galaxy, Spider-Man, and Black Panther, will handle art duties.
  • For a taste of the series' fresh direction, Collider sat down with Rosenberg to talk about good guys, bad guys, the Turtles' New York City stomping grounds, and the incredible artwork of Juann Cabal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

40 Years ago, the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles made their debut. The stars of a black-and-white indie comic by Kevin Eastman and Peter Laird, the quartet of reptilian martial artists were an instant sensation, and within a few years they were the stars of the silver screen, the small screen, and toy stores everywhere. But they've never abandoned their comic book roots: IDW now holds the rights to publish TMNT comics, and after two high-profile runs by writers Jason Aaron and Gene Luen Yang, they're headed in a newly introduced, grittier direction.

The Turtles are in good hands. Starting with January's Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #25, the series will be penned by Matthew Rosenberg, who's written Punisher, Batman, and Spawn, as well as the indie crime comic 4 Kids Walk Into a Bank, while Juann Cabal, a veteran of Guardians of the Galaxy, Spider-Man, and Black Panther, will handle art duties. With TMNT #25 hitting store shelves on January 13, 2027, the last day to reserve a copy at your local comic shop is Monday, November 30.

For a taste of the series' fresh direction, Collider sat down with Rosenberg to talk about good guys, bad guys, the Turtles' New York City stomping grounds, and the incredible artwork of Juann Cabal. We also have an exclusive look at three preview pages from matter #25, which kicks off "War All the Time," an arc that will see the Turtles face off against an army of their deadliest foes. Rosenberg is a longtime fan of both the Turtles and the independent ethos that gave rise to them. When the opportunity came to contribute to their ongoing mythos, Rosenberg jumped at the chance:.

In a recent development, "I fell in love with the Turtles as a small child. The bullies who ran my local comic shop wouldn’t sell me the books I wanted unless I bought the reprints of the original Kevin Eastman and Peter Laird black & white comics. Those books rewired my brain and changed the way I felt about comics completely. They were funnier, angrier, weirder, darker, and just cooler than anything else I’d ever read. So when the folks at IDW asked me if I had any interest I could not have screamed ‘yes’ any faster. Part of the beauty of making comics like this is being a part of the legacy, adding a few stitches to the tapestry that goes back years and will go on after you die. So for this book, these characters who really made me fall in love with different types of comics and stories, taught me what independent art was, and just generally told me it’s cool to be yourself, there is no other book I’d rather be writing.".

"War All the Time" is going to pit the TMNT against a bevy of bad guys, in a story that Rosenberg likens to a collision of classic movie genres. "I really love the old martial arts trope of endless gauntlets of enemies that you see in stuff like Enter the Dragon, Ip Man, or even Kill Bill. Combine all that with the classic people vs. Fresh York City-type stories from the ’80s and ’90s like The Warriors, Death Wish, and After Hours, and I think you have something that speaks to the Turtles because all that stuff was originally in their DNA.".

Rosenberg is from Latest York City, a relative rarity among TMNT writers, and he wants to give the tales of the TMNT a sense of authenticity: "I don’t want to speak ill of other creative teams who have worked on the franchise before, but sometimes it looks like they’re eating pizza from chain restaurants. Sometimes it feels like they only ever hang out in Midtown. Honestly, if all I contribute to the legacy of this franchise is having them argue about which train line to get on, I feel like I’ve done my city proud.".

Four teams, four completely different reasons to put yourself in danger for strangers. This is the roster you actually belong on, what they would want from you, and what it would cost you to stay.

You belong where the stakes are largest and the personalities are loudest. This is a team of people who are all used to being the most notable person in the room, which is exactly why it works and exactly why it keeps nearly falling apart.

You have never had the luxury of being thanked for this. The X-Men protect a world that has never once been comfortable with them existing, and something in you understands exactly why they keep doing it anyway.

Sources indicate that you do not want colleagues, you want your people. The Titans are the team where the friendship came first and the world-saving turned up afterwards as an inconvenient side effect.

You are not asking who to trust. You worked out the answer a while ago and it was nobody in a cape. This is where you go once you have decided the people in charge need watching, and that nobody else is going to do it.

Capturing the group dynamic of the Turtles is key to a successful TMNT run, as four very different personalities bounce off each other. Rosenberg knows it's a challenge, but is confident in his ability to put the Turtles through their paces while mixing fantasy with reality:.

Recent findings suggest that "There have been so many amazing iterations and takes, I don’t feel like it’s my job to reinvent the wheel. I’m taking the pieces I really love — the family dynamic of the four brothers, the youthful energy they have, and their wildly contrasting personalities and putting them in a bit of a pressure cooker. We all have best friends we love and care about. But how do we feel when they keep making jokes while we’re trapped with them on an out-of-control 1 train full of killer mutants with weapons? What do you do when the smartest member of your family comes up with a plan that you don’t think you can all survive? I think what works about the Turtles for all these years is the mix of the incredibly relatable and the wildly surreal, so we’re trying to push both as far as we can.".

It has been revealed that who will they be facing off with? Rosenberg notes that the sheer number of foes makes it less about "who" than "how many," but does note his fondness for one of the team's earliest foes, in his earliest incarnation: the enigmatic, sewer-dwelling, rodent-controlling Rat King, calling him "one of the most unnerving and perfect antagonists.".

Industry observers note that rosenberg also offered praise for his collaborator, Juann Cabal, predicting that he'll go down as "one of the all-time great TMNT artists." He thought the book needed three things from its artist: "1 — An artist who could do action so good audiences wouldn’t even notice if there was dialogue. 2 — character moments and acting so honest that people would forget not just that they were reading a comic, but that they were reading a comic about giant talking turtles. 3 — They needed to look cool." Cabal effortlessly accomplished all three, which you can see for yourself when Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #25 hits shelves on January 13.

According to recent reports, 4 Kids Walk Into a Bank, a crime thriller comic book miniseries by Rosenberg and artist Tyler Boss, first hit shelves in 2016. It centers around a young girl who discovers that her father is planning to rob a bank, and then decides to disrupt his plans by robbing the bank herself. Now, it's going to be a major motion picture, directed by Frankie Shaw (SMILF), adapted for the screen by Rosenberg, and starring Liam Neeson (Schindler's List), Talia Ryder (West Side Story), Whitney Peak (The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping), Jack Dylan Grazer (It), Deacon Phillippe (Motorheads), and Teresa Palmer (The Fall Guy).

Recent findings suggest that ​​​​​​​Rosenberg calls the movie "a throwback to a type of movie I feel like they don’t make as much anymore. A coming-of-age story for screw-ups." He has great praise for Shaw and the film's cast, and thinks that "audiences deserve to see more kids doing crime. It’s good for the soul.".

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #25 will be released on January 13, 2027; the final order cutoff for the issue is November 30. Stay tuned to Collider for future updates.

  • It has been revealed that K-drama fans have much to look forward to in 2027.
  • From dark and gritty K-dramas on Netflix to tooth-rotting romantic comedies airing domestically, there are plenty of exciting projects on the horizon for next year.

Shealyn Scott is a Senior Writer at Screen Rant. She has been writing for the site since 2024, focused on network, reality, streaming, and classic television. A creative writer, journalist, and lover of the written word in all its forms, Shealyn enjoys deconstructing scenes from her favorite demonstrates, using context clues and historical precedent to predict major plot points (which, due to her successful track record, has sparked rumors of clairvoyance). As an award-winning student journalist, Shealyn spent her college years advocating for the humanities while studying English Literature. Her love of storytelling propelled her to expand her degree with minors in Writing and History, believing life to be a mere collection of stories that can be framed in as many ways as a movie scene. As a Senior member of the TV Team, Shealyn treats the series she covers like books, analyzing every line, camera angle, and lighting choice. Thankfully, her personal mission statement lines up perfectly with Screen Rant: every creative work deserves just as much thought from the viewer as it received from its creator.

It has been revealed that K-drama fans have much to look forward to in 2027. The South Korean film industry has soared to upcoming heights in the past ten years, due in part to the success of internationally distributed series on streaming services. With an influx of new viewers, the genre has continued to innovate, with many 2026 K-dramas aiming to impress and contribute to the latest Hallyu wave.

From dark and gritty K-dramas on Netflix to tooth-rotting romantic comedies airing domestically, there are plenty of exciting projects on the horizon for next year. Without a doubt, classic K-drama lovers who enjoy trope-ridden tales, recent fans who seek out boundary-breaking titles, and everyone in-between will be eagerly awaiting an expected 2027 release.

According to recent reports, the Trauma Code: Heroes on Call may be one of the most successful medical K-dramas of the decade thus far. Much like its Western counterparts (The Pitt, House, Grey's Anatomy, etc.), the series follows an ensemble of doctors at a central hospital, including the jaded surgeon who acts as the drama's protagonist.

Between exciting medical cases and some palpable main cast chemistry, the K-drama swiftly became a streaming success on Netflix. Its debut was so impressive, in fact, The Trauma Code: Heroes on Call seasons 2 and 3 entered production simultaneously. The exact release date is unknown, but season 2 will likely drop sometime in 2027.

Recent findings suggest that based on the hit webtoon of the same name, Men of the Harem will center on Empress Latil, a powerful ruler who collects a small ensemble of male concubines. As her love life flourishes, however, Latil will face more political trials than ever.

While there will surely be some steamy romance in accordance to the eponymous harem trope, the main draw of Men of the Harem is its star-studded cast. Bae Suzy is attached as the female lead, while five renowned actors fill out her cabinet of lovers. Sadly, no details have been confirmed beyond the royal K-drama's slated premiere in 2027.

In this upcoming K-drama thriller, fan-favorite male lead Nam Joo-hyuk will take a morally grey turn as antihero Yun Tae-ju, a lawyer desperate to climb the corporate ladder. When he gains access to a mysterious app that grants the user's every wish, his lofty career ambitions finally feel within reach.

In a recent development, nevertheless, everything has a price— a sentiment all forms of media have echoed since "The Monkey's Paw" (1902). Alongside an expert hacker and a leading detective, Tae-ju will seek the truth, though it may cost him everything he desires in the process.

Recent findings suggest that the Twilight Between Us will follow two nobles from opposing families who are forced into an arranged marriage to end a century-long feud. In the north, disgraced heir Mu-yeong (Gang Dong-Won) lives in derision. Similarly, Su-ryeon (Kim Go-eun) is discounted by her kingdom and trapped by outdated royal decrees.

Together, the pair form a strategic bond, but— like any good fake dating scheme— their feelings are bound to become real. Aside from its stacked cast, The Twilight Between Us seems like a brilliant inverse of forbidden love K-dramas, and its 2027–2028 release window can't come quick enough.

Set around the 1988 Seoul Olympics, Born Guilty will follow the journey of Paeng-i (Park Seo-joon) as he unexpectedly inherits a criminal empire. As he stumbles into a massive drug ring, however, the man's greed soon eclipses his conscience.

Born Guilty is one to watch simply for the fact that it's taking an acclaimed romantic lead— Park Seo-joon— and turning him into a complex K-drama villain. Plus, weaving such a sordid tale amidst the real-life chaos of 1980s Korea will make for a fascinating period drama.

Recent findings suggest that another entry on Netflix's 2027 lineup is She, Wolf (previously known by working title Beauty In The Beast). The romantic fantasy K-drama will focus on Min-su (Kim Min-ju), a bright young woman who can secretly transform into a werewolf.

As she tries to adapt to normal life as a college student, Min-su will find herself caught in a love triangle with bad boy wolf-human hybrid Do-ha (Lomon) and apathetic heartthrob Hae-jun (Moon Sang-min). Admittedly, She, Wolf isn't trying to reinvent the wheel, but it will certainly be a must-watch for any rom-com lover.

It has been revealed that unlike the supernatural splendor of She, Wolf, Detective Park Mi Ok will be a K-drama based on a true story. Inspired by the life of the titular Park Mi-ok— a trailblazing homicide detective— the upcoming K-drama will follow the triumphs and tribulations of a woman working in a notoriously male-dominated field.

It has been revealed that while K-dramas based in reality aren't always streaming hits, star actress Kim Ji-won has signed on as the title character, already giving Detective Park Mi Ok a leg-up. Luckily, filming is presently underway, and the K-drama will likely drop on Netflix in the second half of 2027.

Also known as 1/24 Romance, Love O'Clock will be a quintessential office romance K-drama in 2027. After reality TV producer Cha Ju-an (Shin Hae-sun) and former tennis pro Yoo Do-jin (Na In-woo) cross paths on a tech giant retreat, the two inexplicably begin switching bodies for one hour each day.

Recent findings suggest that yet, with Ju-an being a relentless workaholic and Do-jin being a tender-hearted marketing newbie, the pair couldn't be more different. What follows will likely be a heartwarming opposites-attract romance with a captivating fantasy flair.

It has been revealed that similarly, The Dealer seems like a mix of a gripping crime procedural and a superhero K-drama. Expected to release in 2027, the series will follow Jung Geon-hwa (Jung So-min), a dealer at a casino who enters the dark world of gambling after falling victim to a financial scam.

Industry observers note that unbeknownst to her detective boyfriend Choi Woo-seung (Ryu Kyung-soo), however, Geon-hwa has the uncanny ability to detect when someone is lying after she's had alcohol. Consequently, the female lead has, in theory, the perfect way to recoup her life savings— but the scheme may jeopardize her entire relationship.

From the creators of Hotel del Luna comes Grand Galaxy Hotel, a spiritual successor that flips the script of the smash-hit flagship series. In the fantasy romance helmed by the Hong sisters, Eun-ha (Lee Do-Hyun) takes over ownership of a paranormal hotel after the CEO suddenly vanishes.

Although Lee Do-hyun previously appeared in Hotel del Luna as Go Cheong-myeong, his starring role in Grand Galaxy Hotel will be unrelated.

With the help of the human manager Sang-soon (Shin Shi-a), Eun-ha will encounter countless lost souls looking for solace on their way to the afterlife. It will be interesting to see if Grand Galaxy Hotel can go toe-to-toe with its predecessor, but chances are if you enjoyed anything about Hotel del Luna, the newly introduced ghostly K-drama will fit the bill in 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I write a lot about e-readers and e-ink tablets for Lifehacker, and one glitch I'm constantly grappling with is how to write informatively about a bunch of devices that can be quite different in some details, like build or native firmware, and pretty much identical in others, given that literally all e-ink devices use display technology produced by the same Chinese company. (It's called E-Ink.) The best way to do this is to include more video in my articles, but I've lacked a good way to film hands-free so I can easily demonstrate a device's look and feel—until recently.

I recently got an offer to try out a magnetic neck mount from Telesin, a low-cost option to turn my iPhone into a wearable so I can keep my hands free while filming. It's a pretty basic concept, but well-executed: The band that goes around your neck is made of rubber with a firm but flexible core, so you can easily position it to be longer or shorter or at an angle, and the phone mount is on an extending arm with three joints to give you additional options.

Recent findings suggest that I haven't had a chance to film anything for public consumption quite yet, but my testing has already given me some great ideas for how I can use it to show off, say, what it's really like to use a micro-reader in comparison to a full-sized Kindle, as I'll be able to wear it to give a more accurate user's point of view. And right now is a good time to pick one of them up, as many of Telesin's phone and camera accessories (including similar models built to handle an action camera like a GoPro) are discounted for Black Friday; the one I tested is down to $17, or 15% off.

According to recent reports, this won't be the right device for every filming scenario. Though MagSafe holds my iPhone fairly securely, I found that I would accidentally detach it every time I tried to adjust the shooting angle—once even leading me to drop it. That's potentially bad news, as using it may require you to take the phone out of its case if it isn't MagSafe-compatible. (Mine isn't.) But if you're just looking for an inexpensive way to shoot hands-free video in a controlled environment, it could be exactly what you need.

It has been revealed that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

The best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Some other tips are making sure you're not being sold an older or cheaper version and always reading reviews.

Industry observers note that recently, UGREEN introduced a fresh Qi2.2 25W 10000mAh MagSafe battery bank for iPhone. There have been plenty of these, but this one has an interesting new twist: liquid cooling. For Black Friday, it’s on sale for 40% off, making it more affordable than ever.

Industry observers note that on the back of the battery, there’s a window that showcases the liquid within the battery bank moving throughout it. This should help keep it a little bit cooler than most MagSafe battery banks.

In a recent development, UGREEN claims that it’ll be around 18 degrees cooler than usual, and while that’s probably true – it’s worth nothing that it still isn’t a cold battery bank, it’s just cooler than usual. It’ll still feel warm in your hand.

On the bottom of the battery bank, UGREEN integrates a USB-C cable for charging your phone or any other USB-C device that can’t (or you prefer not to) charge wirelessly. I found it a bit handy at times, since of course wireless charging is never as energy efficient as wired charging.

It has been revealed that I will admit, the battery bank is a little bit thick, and the lack of a kickstand is somewhat bothersome at this price point, especially when so many others offer one. That noted, if heat is a concern of yours with MagSafe battery banks, this one will definitely solve that for you.

On the side, it offers a small display for showing battery percentage and charging speed.

One last thing of note: if you’re buying an iPhone Duo, this will stick out from the bottom of the phone. This is true for most MagSafe accessories on iPhone Duo, though.

The UGREEN MagFlow battery bank comes in at $149, which is quite pricey for a MagSafe battery of any kind. For Black Friday, it’s on sale for just $90.23 on Amazon for Prime members, making it much more palatable if you’re looking for a MagSafe battery bank that doesn’t get as hot as the competition.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of Apple’s most beloved products this year was undoubtedly the MacBook Neo. Unlike some of its other budget products, Apple seems interested in updating the MacBook Neo on an annual cycle, and we may get the next MacBook Neo around March.

According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple is targeting the iOS/macOS 27.4 release cycle for the release of the upcoming MacBook Neo, as well as the A19 budget iPad, iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and OLED iPad Air.

Recent findings suggest that while he notes that this cycle runs between February and March, it doesn’t necessarily mean the products will launch on the earlier end of that spectrum. Apple is also expected to release the iPhone Air 2, OLED iPad Air, and a latest iPad Pro within the first half of the year, but they’ll likely come a bit later than the aforementioned products.

As expected, the next MacBook Neo will bump up from the A18 Pro chip with 8GB of RAM to the A19 Pro chip with 12GB of RAM.

In a recent development, apple will also introduce newly introduced colors on the MacBook Neo “frequently,” though it’s unclear if we’ll see that with the next iteration. From the Power On newsletter:.

In a recent development, the other thing I’ve heard is that Apple intends to refresh the MacBook Neo’s colors frequently. We’ll see if that trend starts with the first follow-up.

In a recent development, I’m certainly excited to see the next generation MacBook Neo, especially with 12GB of unified memory. While 8GB is certainly fine, heavy multitaskers will notice it, especially with unoptimized software.

In a recent development, the bigger question is: will the next MacBook Neo have a price increase? With additional RAM included, it feels inevitable.

Hopefully backlit keyboard if they increase price.

Apple increased the price of MacBook Neo from $599 to $699 back in June, and in October the company also silently decreased the education discount by $50, meaning the education price has increased from $499 to $649 since launch.

If there is a price increase, it likely won’t be too major, maybe $50 – leaving the computer at $749. Compared to the rest of the laptop landscape, MacBook Neo would still be a good value. We’ll see what happens.

Industry observers note that having spent much of last summer trying to get rid of the most powerful man on the planet as Lex Luthor in James Gunn's Superman, Nicholas Hoult has turned his attention to a rather different type of criminal enterprise this year, although he's at least had the help of a man who knows a thing or two about making entertaining action movies. Between Bullet Train, Deadpool 2, and Fast & Furious Presents: Hobbs & Shaw, David Leitch has been responsible for some enormously successful action movies over the last decade, but his latest is having a particularly torrid time at the box office. With Thanksgiving weekend upon us, things don't look likely to improve for Hoult and company.

In a recent development, according to the latest theater count figures from The Numbers, Leitch's How to Rob a Bank has officially lost 776 theaters just 12 days after its domestic release. The movie had played in 2,810 theaters across both of its first two weekends, but that number has now been reduced to 2,034, representing a loss of almost 28% of its locations.

Sources indicate that having made just $5.19 million domestically on its opening weekend, How to Rob a Bank suffered a 66% drop in its second weekend, falling out of the domestic box office Top 10 altogether. The movie took in just $263,167 on Monday, meaning that the average theater showing the movie made less than $100 from it across the entire day. The film holds a reported production budget of $50 million against a worldwide gross of just $17 million to date, though the feature still has plenty of time to gain some word of mouth momentum before it arrives at home.

While most people who rob banks would probably prefer that as few people as possible know who they are, the criminals at the center of Leitch's movie have made a point of turning their robberies into online entertainment. Naturally, becoming internet celebrities while committing federal crimes comes with its own set of problems, particularly when an experienced FBI agent enlists the help of a software engineer to track them down. Anything for a bit of social media clout, huh?

Written by Mark Bianculli, the movie features Hoult (Superman) as Ryan, Zoë Kravitz (The Batman) as Reagan Gardner, Anna Sawai (Shōgun) as Emi, Rhenzy Feliz (The Penguin) as Hugo, Pete Davidson (The King of Staten Island) as Vince, John C. Reilly (Step Brothers) as Agent John West, Christian Slater (Mr. Robot) as David Walton, and Tati Gabrielle (Uncharted) as Skyler Deluca.

How to Rob a Bank is currently playing in over 2,000 theaters. Stay tuned to Collider for all the latest box office news and updates.

Five recent tech outages were not due to AI; the next round will be

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Five major tech outages in quick succession earlier this month led to speculation that they were connected, with some inevitably believing them to be AI-related.
  • That wasn’t the case, but the US Director of National Intelligence is one of a number of experts warning that we should expect AI-powered outages in the near future ….
  • Earlier this month saw five tech outages, one after the other.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Five major tech outages in quick succession earlier this month led to speculation that they were connected, with some inevitably believing them to be AI-related.

That wasn’t the case, but the US Director of National Intelligence is one of a number of experts warning that we should expect AI-powered outages in the near future ….

Earlier this month saw five tech outages, one after the other. A widespread Microsoft 365 outage occurred when two unrelated issues coincided. The next day saw a nationwide ground stop of US air traffic due to a communication problem affecting all air traffic control centers. A few days later, a bug in a Chase bank system saw disruption not only to the bank itself, but also other banks where Chase was a party to a transaction. Many Apple services went offline later the same week, with retail stores also affected. Finally, United Airlines had its own widespread IT outage that grounded a significant number of flights.

Each had their own unrelated causes, with the White House stating that rumors of an AI-facilitated systemic attack by a hostile state were false.

According to recent reports, however, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has warned that we should expect future tech outages as a result of attacks facilitated by AI-discovered vulnerabilities. CNBC reports him issuing the warning on CNN’s State of the Union.

The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road.

You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot.

We already saw an example of this last month when a vulnerability discovered in PHP saw a significant number of websites being taken offline.

Microsoft President Brad Smith says it isn’t just a question of bad actors exploiting vulnerabilities discovered by AI, but companies rushing to patch these may inadvertently cause systems to fail, as Newsweek reports.

What AI did earlier this year was basically make it much easier for people to find vulnerabilities in code, and then you can either use that knowledge to patch the code, or if you’re a bad actor, you can use that knowledge to try to hack into systems.

Especially when you have older infrastructure, especially when you’re trying to patch at such a pace, especially when you have to go so fast that you can’t take as much time to test what you’re changing in the code, you do increase the risk of something going wrong.

Major IT failures look set to be a routine event in the coming weeks and months.

The tech giant is even so bold as to say the Series 12 has the most accurate heart rate monitor on a wearable.

The S11 isn't only responsible for these new heart rate features, however. In addition to running the same watchOS 27 features as other compatible Apple Watches, the S11 on the Series 12 can run Audio Intelligence, Apple's new suite of AI-powered audio features. That includes "Live Rewind," which lets you see a transcript of the last 15 seconds of an in-person conversation, and "Siri Recaps," which displays summaries of your conversations throughout the day. Finally, the other major advantage with the Series 12 is Ceramic Shield 2. This is a display upgrade that Apple typically reserves for more premium Apple Watch finishes, but this year, the aluminum Series 12 gets it as well. That means the watch should be more durable against scratches and cracks, without you having to upgrade to the more expensive model.

Recent findings suggest that how much you'll save on a Series 12 depends on the size, color, and model. At this time, Amazon is selling certain colors of the 42mm Series 12 for $299, while certain colors of the 46mm option run $449 (also marked down by $100). You can also save on the cellular models as well: The 42mm option is right now $429 (down from $499), while the 46mm model is $449 (down from $549).

If You Loved 'The Good Daughter,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1064 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are plenty of reasons Peacock’s The Good Daughter is so damn watchable.
  • Dark Places has seriously buried secrets.
  • Like The Good Daughter, Dark Places is anchored by a sibling relationship reshaped by the impact of horrifying violence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are plenty of reasons Peacock’s The Good Daughter is so damn watchable. The performances, for one—Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy are terrific as estranged sisters Sam and Charlotte Quinn. But it’s also a great story, tracing the corrosive effect of a years-ago trauma on the women and their lawyer father (Brendan Gleeson) amid the slow revelation of many extremely dark secrets. If you want more of that flavor of trauma-driven drama with a tight focus on family bonds, there’s one movie you should watch: 2015's Dark Places.

You want buried secrets? Dark Places has seriously buried secrets. Adapted from the Gillian Flynn novel, the film follows Libby Day (Charlize Theron), who survived the mass murder of her family in 1985. The crime is blamed on her brother Ben, a moody loner whose conviction was based in large part on Libby’s own testimony. For a long time, Libby is financially sustained by donations from people who sympathize with her plight, but three decades after the murders, the money has dried up, and Libby is desperate—so desperate, she agrees to help out a “true crime” club that believes her brother is innocent and is working toward his release.

Like The Good Daughter, Dark Places is anchored by a sibling relationship reshaped by the impact of horrifying violence. Libby and Ben’s experience mirrors Sam and Charlie’s in many ways, including in the way both Libby and Ben carry secrets for years after the terrible events that took family from them. The stories are also both compelling mysteries, slowly revealing the shocking truths behind one horrific night, and ultimately allowing the characters to better understand one another.

Sources indicate that dark Places also explores the insular, suffocating nature of small-town life, and how rumor and gossip become a poisonous presence in people’s lives. Libby, Ben, Sam, and Charlie all have to deal with others' assumptions and revelations that they've been betrayed by those closest to them, leading to powerful resolutions. If you loved The Good Daughter, you’ll love this movie. Stream Dark Places on The Roku Channel or Kanopy, or rent it on Prime Video.

Want more stories about family dynamics around secrets, violence, and explosive emotional confrontations? Here are a few more movies fans of The Good Daughter are bound to enjoy.

It has been revealed that there’s no violent crime at the heart of this slow-burn drama—just an explosive chaos agent named Kym, played by Anne Hathaway. If your favorite aspect of The Good Daughter was the relationship between sisters Sam and Charlie, then this movie is perfect. Released from rehab to attend her sister’s wedding, Kym is self-hating, angry, and haunted by a terrible event from her childhood. Her sister, Rachel (Rosemary DeWitt), is welcoming, but has never truly forgiven Kym, and the simmering tension between the sisters and the rest of the family drives a drama that you won’t be able to look away from. Stream Rachel Getting Married on Apple TV or rent it on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that if you really vibed on the Southern setting, the slow-burn mystery, and the exploration of flawed justice in the modern age depicted in The Good Daughter, check out Where the Crawdads Sing. It’s a slower, dreamier rumination on rural life, violence and its cost, and small-town justice, but it hits the same sweet spot in its story about a woman named Kya (Daisy Edgar-Jones) who was raised in an isolated house in the swamps of North Carolina. Accused in 1969 of a murder, Kya’s story stretches back to her childhood, when she’s slowly abandoned by her entire family, leaving her at age seven to survive on her own. Ostracized as the “swamp girl” by the town, Kya fights to live her life and be loved while facing the unwanted—and violently persistent—attention of the murder victim. It’s about broken families, deeply buried secrets, and what we do to survive. Stream Where the Crawdads Sing on Hulu or rent it on Prime Video.

The Good Daughter is about life in a small, Southern town, family trauma, and the legal system—which makes A Time to Kill the perfect movie to watch when you finish the show. When a Black man’s daughter is sexually assaulted in Mississippi and her attackers—local members of the Ku Klux Klan—look likely to go free, he violently and publicly murders them. Local lawyer Jake Brigance (Matthew McConaughey) takes on the case, assisted by law student Ellen Roark (Sandra Bullock). They face violent opposition, withering racism, and an unfair legal system that echoes the environment in The Good Daughter in ways fans will appreciate. Stream A Time to Kill on YoutTube or rent it on Prime Video.

The Dry might be as close as you can get to The Good Daughter in terms of tone and story. Although set in Australia instead of the American South, The Dry is a story driven by past crimes and buried secrets in a rural setting just like the show. Twenty years ago, Federal agent Aaron Falk (Eric Bana) fled his hometown when he was suspected of the murder of his girlfriend. When his childhood friend, Luke, appears to have murdered his wife and young son before killing himself, he returns to investigate. The slow revelation of two mysteries—one in the past and one simmering in the drought-stricken present—makes this an ideal companion film to the show. Stream The Dry on The Roku Channel, Kanopy, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, set in Boston instead of the South, and focused on male friendships instead of a sisters’ bond, Mystic River nevertheless nails the same atmosphere of dread as The Good Daughter. In 1975, boyhood friends Jimmy, Dave, and Sean are traumatized when Dave is abducted and assaulted by two men. In 1990, the three men remain connected in their Boston neighborhood—Jimmy (Sean Penn) is an ex-convict still connected to local crime, Sean (Kevin Bacon) is a State Police detective, and Dave (Tim Robbins) is a blue-collar worker still haunted by his experience. When Jimmy’s daughter is found murdered and Dave seems implicated, Sean and Jimmy launch investigations from either side of the law, with Dave’s fate hanging in the balance. The ending is powerfully brutal, but this story of secrets and suspicion will resonate with fans of the show. Rent Mystic River on Prime Video.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, nvidia has confirmed that disgraced CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated to the role, effective immediately. The company’s share price jumped more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also making significant gains.

It stated that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so ….

Recent findings suggest that huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy became the main headline news in the tech press after coming to light at the end of last month. The Newly introduced York Times broke the story on October 29, citing it then as “a close relationship.” Nvidia initially denied that the relationship was anything out of the ordinary.

In a recent development, that changed on November 8 when Huang publicly admitted to the affair. Nvidia’s shares dropped 5%, and the company’s board of directors opened an independent investigation. Further details emerged over the following days. Things got even worse when the same paper reported that Huang had also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him.

That led to Huang being fired resigning on November 12.

Recent findings suggest that money over country. This is government intervention.

It has been revealed that despite putting the manufacturer at enormous risk and initially lying to its board of directors, there were calls in some quarters for Huang to be reinstated. He responded by saying that he would be “honored” to return if asked to do so.

The board of directors, however, stated that it had no intention of inviting him back.

Nvidia’s chair Harvey Jones said: “The board does not intend to reinstate him.”.

That changed today, with the company making the announcement in a press release.

Nvidia today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.

In a recent development, “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Organization. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” remarked Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”.

Recent findings suggest that as previously announced, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

The organization’s stock price jumped by more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also up per Yahoo Finance.

Nvidia shares soared more than 30% Monday morning […] The S&P 500 (^GSPC) rose 4.5% following seven straight days of declines. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) jumped more than 1,200 points to recover by 2.5% following its worst week since the COVID-related sell-off in 2020. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) rallied 7%.

#200212. Will Siri AI threaten Apple’s environmental target, given Google and Meta admissions?

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (995 w)
📖 Baca

Will Siri AI threaten Apple’s environmental target, given Google and Meta admissions?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (995 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that I think Apple can reasonably claim to be the leading tech giant when it comes to its environmental credentials.
  • All of this could potentially be put at risk by the manufacturer’s ambitions for Siri AI, however, as Meta joins Google in admitting it is now unlikely to meet its own 2030 net zero promise, thanks to the huge power demands of the data centers powering its AI services ….
  • Apple’s environmental record isn’t entirely perfect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I think Apple can reasonably claim to be the leading tech giant when it comes to its environmental credentials. It has led the way with its use of renewable energy, made significant strides with carbon-neutral production, and removed plastic from all its packaging.

All of this could potentially be put at risk by the manufacturer’s ambitions for Siri AI, however, as Meta joins Google in admitting it is now unlikely to meet its own 2030 net zero promise, thanks to the huge power demands of the data centers powering its AI services ….

Apple’s environmental record isn’t entirely perfect. For example, when it claimed that the Apple Watch Series 9 and Ultra 2 were carbon neutral back in 2023, that claim was described as “bogus,” with the EU banning Apple from repeating it. The organization has also been criticized for pushing a relentless annual iPhone cycle, encouraging frequent upgrades.

Overall, however, Apple has first-rate credentials when it comes to the environment. It was way back in 2018 when the company hit its goal of running its own operations off 100% renewable energy. This includes all Apple facilities, from Apple Park through data centers to its worldwide retail store network.

I said at the time that using more environmentally friendly packaging should be the manufacturer’s next priority, and it has indeed made great progress with this over the years, succeeding in removing all plastic packaging earlier this year.

After its own operations, Apple set about trying to tackle the power usage of its manufacturing partners. Back in 2020, the tech giant set a goal of having its entire supply chain be carbon neutral by 2030. Just four years later, Apple noted it was 95% of the way there.

Sources indicate that the company also helps fund and support a wide range of environmental initiatives around the world. Just a few examples include conservation in China’s national parks, environmental protection and carbon removal in Australia and Latest Zealand, and helping to fund the build-out of renewable energy capacity in India.

Potentially, however, the vast energy demands of the data centers powering AI services could put its 2030 goal at risk. Other tech giants have already admitted that it may lead them to fail to hit their own renewable energy promises.

Back in 2024, for example, Google CEO Sundar Pichai said that the AI boom was “challenging” to the company’s 2030 carbon-free goal. CNET reports that Meta is now also admitting that it may fail to hit the same target.

Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the firm is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline.”.

Notably, a lot of Siri’s most advanced AI capabilities are right now powered by Google’s Gemini models.

In a recent development, at the same 2024 event where Google expressed doubts, Apple reiterated its commitment to its 2030 target. Then-CEO Tim Cook repeated this assurance later the same year, although admitted it would be challenging.

More challenges, yes. But are we coming off the goal? No, definitely not. With more data centers, you use more renewable energy, and we’ve built that muscle now […] I feel very good about 2030.

In the tech giant’s most recent environmental progress report, it said that it was was still using 100% renewable energy despite using over 2.5 billion kWh of electricity to power its data centers.

According to recent reports, we’re proud that 100 percent of that electricity came from renewable sources including solar, wind, and low-impact hydropower. To cover our needs, we build our own renewable power projects and work with utilities to purchase clean energy from locally obtained resources. We’re staying at 100 percent even as Apple’s data center capacity continues to grow.

The same report said the company had achieved zero water use for cooling at its latest data centers.

At our three newest data centers, we use high-efficiency air-cooled chillers instead of water-cooled systems, resulting in zero water use for cooling.

However, the greatest challenge for Apple lies ahead. The reason that Google and Meta are now backtracking on their promises is that both companies now have massive AI capabilities. As yet, Apple does not.

Sources indicate that what happens as Apple expands Siri AI capabilities as usage increases, and as the tech giant moves into agentic AI features? Is it realistic for the company to maintain its 100% track record with vastly greater data center energy usage?

Greenpeace expressed its own doubts earlier this year.

Recent findings suggest that “AI will be the defining test of Apple’s climate commitments,” spokesperson Avex Li claims. “To preserve Tim Cook’s environmental legacy, the tech giant will need to show that AI growth can be accommodated within its existing climate commitments through absolute emissions reductions, additional renewable energy investment, and longer-lasting products.”.

Apple did not respond directly but merely pointed to its past statements and most recent environmental progress report.

I don’t doubt the tech giant’s desire to maintain its track record, but if Apple does join the likes of Google and Meta in becoming a major AI player, sticking to its 2030 timing is going to become increasingly difficult.

According to recent reports, do you think Apple will succeed? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, coros has unveiled the Vertix 4, an “expedition-focused” patch to the Vertix 2 and 2S. Coros claims it pairs the brand's brightest display yet with long battery life, and after unboxing it myself, I can definitely say it has a more refined feel that could indeed suit the office as well as the summit.

This watch is being marketed as a major step up from the Vertix 2S, with an AMOLED display, a more refined design, satellite maps and, for the first time on a Coros watch, a built-in flashlight. The Vertix 4 will be available to buy starting on Black Friday, Nov. 27, but it won't exactly be at a discount: It costs $799, a $100 increase over the Vertix 2S.

In a recent development, that price does still undercut the latest Garmin Fenix 9 line-up, which starts at $999, though some rivals are cheaper still. For instance, the Suunto Vertical 2 steel model costs $599, and the Garmin Fenix 8 is right now on sale for $749.99 at Amazon.

I've only just started testing the Vertix 4 and haven't even had enough time to get through its substantial battery life, but I can share some first impressions, particularly in how it compares with the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro that debuted earlier this year.

Built-in flashlights have become a must-have feature on premium sports watches, and now the Vertix 4 is the first Coros watch to get one. Coros has departed from the usual layout, though. Garmin, Suunto and Amazfit put the light on top of the watch, but Coros places it on the side, between the digital dial and the back button.

According to recent reports, previous Vertix watches used a memory-in-pixel (MIP) display. MIP has advantages, most notably longer battery life, but I know I much prefer the vibrant display on AMOLED screens, like on the Vertix 4. It is the biggest visual change and a large part of why the watch looks more premium than its predecessors.

Coros claims up to 30 days in watch mode, or 10 days with the screen always on. It also quotes 48 hours of multi-band GPS tracking with the screen always on. I haven't had time to test these claims properly, so stay tuned.

Coros watches are high-quality sports watches, but don't expect to find all the little lifestyle features you've come to expect on a more traditional smartwatch:.

In a recent development, music: It can store tracks, but only files you drag and drop onto the watch. It doesn't pair with streaming services.

Payments: There is no NFC payment support.

Watch faces: Customization is more limited than on rivals.

Recent findings suggest that on paper, the Vertix 4 looks like a significant upgrade: a better display, a more attractive design, a flashlight and satellite maps, at a price well below the Fenix 9 line-up. The $100 increase and cheaper alternatives like the Suunto Vertical 2 and discounted Fenix 8 will matter to some buyers, as will the limited smart features.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Netflix is always adding upcoming movies to its already-large library, but the flip side is that each month, it also removes a bunch of familiar favorites. So, while you might prioritize the new Netflix additions, it's worth making time to watch some soon-to-depart movies while you still have the chance.

It has been revealed that on December 1, 2026, Netflix is set to remove 37 movies from its library. This includes my favorite movie of all time (and its equally five-star sequel), a beloved '80s coming-of-age story, and a very intense thriller that stars the late, great Patrick Stewart. And these are just some of the movies that are leaving.

Recent findings suggest that that's a big number, which is why I've combed through the list and picked out a more manageable selection of five great movies you need to watch before they wave Netflix goodbye. Plus, I've also included the full list of movies being removed from Netflix on December 1, if you want to pick your own.

In the headline, I called “Alien” a “sci-fi masterpiece,” and if anything, that’s underplaying my love of this titan of the genre. It’s my favorite movie of all time, and it started my favorite media franchise. This 1979 horror introduced the world to the Xenomorph, and the terrifying alien creature has been a staple of pop culture since. Directed by Ridley Scott, and with a star-making turn from Sigourney Weaver, it’s more than worthy of its enduring legacy.

The premise is simple: a group of deep-space truckers is awoken from hypersleep when their ship alerts them to a strange transmission on a nearby planet. The source of the signal brings pure terror onboard, as they encounter a lethal predator, perfectly formed to kill. The almost-as-good sequel, “Aliens,” is also leaving Netflix on Dec. 1, so make sure you stream them both quickly. Trust me, they make for the perfect sci-fi double-bill.

Watch "Alien" on Netflix until December 1.

In a recent development, the entertainment world mourned the great Patrick Stewart last month, so it feels like a fitting time to recommend “Green Room.” This thriller is noteworthy because Stewart plays against type. He’s not playing a hero or a warm father figure, but instead the veteran actor plays the leader of a neo-Nazi group. And he’s chilling! The movie was also the final film released in Anton Yelchin’s lifetime. The actor tragically passed away in 2016, at just 27.

It has been revealed that in “Green Room,” members of a scrappy punk band are booked to play a dive bar, which they soon discover is actually a clubhouse for a neo-Nazi group. After witnessing a member of the group commit murder, they are trapped in the green room backstage and have to fight their way out. Also starring Imogen Poots and Callum Turner, “Green Room” is fast-paced and very loud, not to mention splattered with fake blood. It’s a hoot, and seriously intense.

Watch "Green Room" on Netflix until December 1.

Netflix is removing “The Karate Kid”, its two original sequels released in 1986 and 1989, and the 2010 remake soon. I have a soft spot for the remake (please, flame me in the comments!), but I can’t deny that the 1984 original is the true classic in the bunch. One of the most iconic and beloved coming-of-age movies of all time, this flick is charming, relatable, and very good fun.

Daniel LaRusso (Ralph Macchio) moves from Newly introduced Jersey to Los Angeles, California, and finds the transition tough. Things only get worse when he’s harassed by the students of the Cobra Kai dojo, led by Johnny Lawrence (William Zabka). But Daniel learns to stand up for himself when his apartment's handyman, Mr. Miyagi (Pat Morita), takes him under his wing and teaches him karate. This gives Daniel confidence and a new perspective.

Watch "The Karate Kid" on Netflix until December 1.

Recent findings suggest that meg Ryan and Tom Hanks are a classic romantic-comedy pairing, having starred in “Joe Versus the Volcano,” “You’ve Got Mail” and “Sleepless in Seattle.” Each flick sees them playing characters who fall in love across the movie’s runtime. It’s 1993’s “Sleepless in Seattle” that’s waving goodbye to Netflix next week, but make sure to give it a watch before then if you want a charming rom-com. Yes, it’s sappy, but I dare you not to get emotional.

Industry observers note that architect Sam Baldwin (Hanks) moves from Chicago to Seattle with his eight-year-old son, Jonah (Ross Malinger), after the death of his wife. Aware his father is struggling to come to terms with the loss, Jonah calls a national radio station to find his dad a new wife. Listening in is Annie Reed (Ryan), a Baltimore reporter, who falls for Sam, despite being engaged. It’s a very 1990s plot for a movie; these days, Jonah would have probably just posted a TikTok.

Watch "Sleepless in Seattle" on Netflix until December 1.

According to recent reports, jessica Chastain recently starred in the Netflix Original thriller “Heartland,” which, according to many critics (including TG’s Alix Blackburn), is a bit of a misfire. However, one Chastain-led movie that does hit the mark is “Zero Dark Thirty,” a sprawling political thriller from director Kathryn Bigelow, which was nominated for a clutch of Oscars including Best Picture. Its chunky 157-minute runtime might put some viewers off, but give the film your full attention, and you’ll be richly rewarded with a gripping war movie.

Chastain plays Maya Krauser, a fictional CIA intelligence analyst, with a singular focus. Her mission is to find terrorist leader Osama bin Laden, and her determination borders on and then crosses over into obsession. Set over multiple years, “Zero Dark Thirty” chronicles the decade-long manhunt for the man responsible for the world-altering September 11 attacks.

Watch "Zero Dark Thirty" on Netflix until December 1.

#200205. iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (880 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5mac ↗ Open Full Page

iOS 27 basically turns your iPhone and AirPods into an Apple Watch at the gym

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (880 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that gymKit has been one of Apple Watch’s smartest fitness features since it debuted in 2017.
  • With iOS 27, Apple is expanding that idea beyond Apple Watch.
  • I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that gymKit has been one of Apple Watch’s smartest fitness features since it debuted in 2017. Tap your watch to compatible gym equipment, and Apple Watch shares your heart rate while the machine sends back metrics like distance, incline, pace, and calories.

With iOS 27, Apple is expanding that idea beyond Apple Watch. I tested the new GymKit on iPhone and AirPods Pro 3 ($149, reg. $249) experience with a GymKit-compatible treadmill. It basically gives you the Apple Watch GymKit workout tracking experience, just without the watch. This could be useful in a lot of scenarios.

The setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment.

Once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

Recent findings suggest that as a side note: Apple Watch has more accurate treadmill workout tracking as part of watchOS 27. GymKit remains the gold standard for accurate data, though.

Recent findings suggest that gymKit also avoids two awkward gym habits. You don’t need to hold the treadmill’s metal heart-rate contacts while jogging. You also do not need to wear a Bluetooth heart-rate strap.

Sources indicate that airPods Pro 3 become the heart-rate source (and likely your podcast or music audio source as well). iPhone becomes the workout computer, which you can monitor during your workout. And the treadmill fills in the machine data while providing the surface for walking or running.

In a recent development, apple has been moving more fitness features onto iPhone for years. iOS first made the Fitness app useful without Apple Watch as Apple Fitness+ leaned into iPhone as an entry point. AirPods Pro 3 pushed that further as the first AirPods with heart-rate tracking, after Apple tested the idea with Powerbeats Pro 2.

It has been revealed that iOS 27 brings those pieces together. GymKit on iPhone shouldn’t replace Apple Watch for people who wear one every day. Instead, it’s a great backup when your Apple Watch is dead, charging, or left at home.

It also gives iPhone and AirPods users a taste of the Apple Watch experience, which could attract future Apple Watch customers.

In testing with iOS 27 beta 1, my Exercise ring didn’t update as I worked out without wearing Apple Watch. But after I put my watch back on, the Exercise ring caught up, and the workout appeared in Fitness with the right data.

My sample 16-minute treadmill walk showed 0.66 miles, 65 active calories, 97 total calories, 32 feet of elevation gain, and a 115 BPM average heart rate, just like if I’d worn an Apple Watch.

I had been getting the impression that gym equipment manufacturers had been abandoning GymKit support - if they ever had done so initially. I even got the impression that the majority of equipment in Apple's own onsite Gym at the Apple Park may not have supported it - at least originally.

Does Apple have a webpage listing compatible brands and models? Like they do/did for HomeKit.

According to recent reports, what is other people perception? Any rowing machines that support it?

…checks - surprisingly it looks like Peloton do support it on their bikes.

Industry observers note that if I tried to use GymKit on iPhone without AirPods, the iPhone disconnected when the workout started because it had no heart-rate source. If I tried to start GymKit from iPhone while wearing Apple Watch, iOS pointed me back to the Workout app on Apple Watch instead, though you can continue without using the watch.

AirPods heart-rate permission also matters. You can manage it in Settings under your AirPods settings and privacy options. I had turned it off, mostly as a theoretical battery-saving move, but this test convinced me to turn it back on. AirPods Pro 3 can also work with Apple Watch to provide the best available heart-rate data.

Sources indicate that gymKit on iPhone is one of those iOS 27 features that sounds small until it solves a real problem. If Apple Watch is your default workout tracker, it probably stays that way.

But if your watch dies or you forget it at home, iPhone plus AirPods Pro 3 can now log a treadmill workout with real heart-rate data and real treadmill metrics.

#200204. Breaking: Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI
